attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence. Phrasing it as what 'many onlookers recognize' still endorses the view ('for what they are').

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase of a present-tense characterisation of GPT-3-like systems. Note that 'real coherence' and 'very little' are evaluative and have no thresholds.

contract.note: The plain reading of memorization, coherence and comprehension is ordinary and not stretched. But the outcome depends on thresholds for 'spectacular' and 'very little' that the speaker never supplied, and on the evaluator's chosen 2022 window.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own 2020 paper lists coherence loss and comprehension gaps alongside high quality. It is company documentation from before the target period and does not test the 'very little' threshold.
Scarecrow (ACL 2022, first public 2021) finds fluent GPT-3 text with measurable error gaps. Fluency is not comprehension, and the study does not establish target-period behavior.
A 2022 memorization study of GPT-Neo/GPT-J and GPT-2 baselines. It does not measure GPT-3, so it cannot settle 'spectacular at memorization' for GPT-3.

reviews.rationale: No item directly measures GPT-3 memorization, sustained coherence or comprehension in Jan–Jul 2022 against the contract's conditions. e1 shows limits alongside strengths but is from 2020. e2 covers fluency only. e3 covers other models. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense observation that negation is a major weak spot for current neural networks. The normalisation preserves the scope.

contract.note: Reading 'major sore spot' as substantial, recurring difficulty when negation matters, not universal failure, is ordinary and fair. Limiting it to language models in 2022 is reasonable given the context.

evidence.note: ACL 2022 study (preprint March 2022): RoBERTa scores substantially lower when negation matters across several tasks (e.g. QNLI 0.67 vs 0.92). These are subset comparisons for one model, not matched pairs.
ACL 2022 pragmatic study gives a 'much more optimistic' picture of negation understanding. This is material counterevidence, but the abstract does not show reliable handling across varied tasks.

reviews.rationale: e1, a contemporaneous primary study, shows substantial, recurring performance drops where negation matters, across several tasks. This meets the support condition. e2 offers a more optimistic pragmatic view but does not meet the contradiction condition. Support is modest: it rests on one model and non-matched subsets.
